title: Admin - Content Management - Edit Informational Page - Functional Test Plan
overview: Functional testing of the Admin Content Management - Edit Informational Page feature on the Y4J platform. This feature allows Admins to edit existing informational pages via a modal with pre-loaded Title and Content fields. Changes are saved with 'Save Changes' button, and the last updated date and admin name are automatically updated. Covers happy path, pre-loading, save behavior, metadata updates, and error handling.

testCases.title: Clicking Edit opens the edit modal
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Content Management page is loaded with at least one existing informational page.
steps: Navigate to Content Management page
Find an existing informational page in the list
Click the 'Edit' button on that page
Observe the modal behavior
expectedResults: The 'Edit' button is visible on each page in the list
Clicking Edit opens an edit modal/dialog
The modal contains Page Title and Page Content fields
The modal has a 'Save Changes' button
The modal has a way to close/cancel
testCases.postconditions: Edit modal is open for the selected page

testCases.title: Edit modal contains Page Title and Page Content fields
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Edit modal is open for an existing page.
steps: Open the edit modal for any page
Observe the form fields present
expectedResults: A Page Title input field is present
A Page Content field is present (textarea or rich text editor)
Both fields have visible labels
A 'Save Changes' button is visible
testCases.postconditions: Both required fields are visible in the edit modal

testCases.title: Existing content loads automatically in the edit modal
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A page with known title and content exists.
steps: Navigate to Content Management page
Find a page with a known title (e.g., 'About Us')
Click Edit on that page
Observe the Title and Content fields in the modal
expectedResults: The Page Title field is pre-populated with the existing title
The Page Content field is pre-populated with the existing content
The pre-loaded data matches exactly what is displayed in the page list
No empty fields — existing data loads automatically
testCases.postconditions: Edit modal shows the current page data

testCases.title: Admin can update the page title
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Edit modal is open with pre-loaded content.
steps: Open the edit modal for a page
Clear the existing title
Enter a new title (e.g., 'Updated Page Title')
Click 'Save Changes'
expectedResults: The title field is editable
The new title can be entered
Save completes successfully
The page list shows the updated title
testCases.postconditions: Page title is updated in the list

testCases.title: Admin can update the page content
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Edit modal is open with pre-loaded content.
steps: Open the edit modal for a page
Modify the existing content (add, remove, or change text)
Click 'Save Changes'
expectedResults: The content field is editable
Changes to content are accepted
Save completes successfully
The updated content is persisted

testCases.title: Clicking Save Changes updates the page successfully
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Edit modal is open with changes made.
steps: Make changes to the title or content
Click 'Save Changes' button
Observe the result
expectedResults: The save operation completes successfully
A success notification may be displayed
The modal closes after successful save
The page list reflects the updated content
No page refresh is required
testCases.postconditions: Page is updated and modal is closed

testCases.title: Last updated date is updated after save
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A page has just been edited and saved.
steps: Edit a page and save changes
Observe the page entry in the list
Check the 'Last Updated' date
expectedResults: The 'Last Updated' date shows today's date/time
The date is updated automatically by the system
The previous date is replaced with the current date
The date format is consistent with other entries
testCases.postconditions: Last updated date reflects the edit time

testCases.title: Admin name is updated after save
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin (pv@mailto.plus). A page has just been edited and saved.
steps: Edit a page and save changes
Observe the page entry in the list
Check the 'Last Updated By' or editor name field
expectedResults: The admin name/email who made the edit is displayed
It shows the current logged-in admin (e.g., 'pv@mailto.plus' or 'Admin Name')
The field is updated automatically by the system
It reflects who last edited the page
testCases.postconditions: Editor name reflects the current admin

testCases.title: Closing modal without saving discards changes
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Edit modal is open with unsaved changes.
steps: Open the edit modal for a page
Make changes to the title or content
Close the modal without clicking 'Save Changes' (click X, Escape, or Cancel)
Observe the page in the list
expectedResults: The modal closes without saving
The page in the list shows the original (unchanged) title and content
No changes are persisted to the backend
No error messages are shown
Re-opening the edit modal shows the original content
testCases.postconditions: Changes are discarded when modal is closed without saving

testCases.title: Save fails due to network error - error notification shown
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Edit modal is open. Network/API is configured to fail.
steps: Make changes to the page
Click 'Save Changes' (with network failure simulated)
Observe the error handling
expectedResults: An error notification is displayed (e.g., 'Failed to save changes. Please try again.')
The modal remains open so the user can retry
The original page content is not corrupted
The user can attempt to save again after the error

testCases.title: Updated page persists after page refresh
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A page has been edited and saved.
steps: Edit a page and save changes
Refresh the browser page (F5)
Find the edited page in the list
expectedResults: After refresh, the page shows the updated title/content
The changes are persisted to the backend
The last updated date and admin name are still correct
No data loss occurs on refresh

testCases.title: Title cannot be saved empty
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Edit modal is open.
steps: Open the edit modal
Clear the title field completely
Click 'Save Changes'
expectedResults: The form does NOT submit with empty title
A validation error is displayed (e.g., 'Title is required')
The modal remains open for correction

testCases.title: Content cannot be saved empty
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Edit modal is open.
steps: Open the edit modal
Clear the content field completely
Click 'Save Changes'
expectedResults: The form does NOT submit with empty content
A validation error is displayed (e.g., 'Content is required')
The modal remains open for correction
